brief: Goldman Sachs' mid-day note (17 Sep 2026) frames markets after the hawkish September 16 FOMC meeting, where Fed Chair Warsh flagged inflation risk and more hikes. Stocks initially sold off, then rallied Thursday with bonds as oil pulled back. GS calls this a possible dead-cat bounce or a sign markets trust the Fed's inflation fight. GS now expects an October hike, keeps its 3.25-3.5% neutral-rate view, and adds a third 2028 cut to its forecast. Its 3.2% year-end PCE forecast, 20bp below the Fed's own 3.4%, is the key test: if correct, GS thinks that is enough for the Fed to stop hiking after October and start considering cuts, especially if growth or the labor market slows. Despite the hiking cycle, GS still expects the bull market to continue on solid earnings, echoing Oppenheimer's constructive-but-measured stance. Separately, GS ties higher rates to intense AI-driven global demand for capital, record equity issuance and record IG credit forecasts, concluding competition for capital may keep rates higher for longer. Also notes mixed Philly Fed and housing data, with GDP tracking raised to 3.2%.
